title: WPMS/2583/2023 of SUNDER SINGH Vs DISTRICT MAGISTRATE , UTTARKASHI

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2583 of 2023
Sunder Singh .............Petitioner
Versus

Present:-
Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Mohit Maulekhi, Brief Holder for respondent
no.1.
Mr. B.S. Negi, Advocate for respondent no.2.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
By means of the instant application, the
petitioner seeks the following reliefs:-
i) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of Mandamus calling for
the records and directing the respondents to forthwith make
payment of petitioner in lieu of the satisfactory completion of work
performed by the petitioner.
ii) Issue any other order or direction which this Hon'ble Court may
deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.
iii) Award cost of the petition.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.

2
3. It is the case of the petitioner that he
undertook certain works given to him by the respondent
no.2 in the year 2020, but he has not been paid the bills.
On 20.09.2023, when the matter was taken up, the Court
requested the learned State counsel to get instruction in
the matter particularly, as to whether the claim, as made
by the petitioner, is admitted to the respondent
authorities. And if not, what is the dispute?
4. Today, learned counsel appearing for the
respondent no.2 would submit that the claim of the
petitioner is not admitted to the respondent no.2. He
would submit that the petitioner did not complete the
work; therefore, payment has not been made.
5. Instant petition has been filed claiming for the
construction that according to the petitioner, he
undertook. The claim is not admitted. It is disputed by
the respondent no.2 on the ground that the petitioner did
not complete the work. There are factual disputes
involved in this petition, which may not be decided in the
instant writ petition. The petitioner is always at liberty to
seek such liberty under the civil law, as is permissible.

3
6. Having considered, this Court is of the view
that there is no reason to make any interference in this
petition. Accordingly, the petition deserves to be
dismissed at the stage of admission itself.
7. The petition is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 26.09.2023
Sanjay
